subjectLine: Cisco ISE CVSS 10.0 Zero-Day Under Active Attack, Check Point Root RCE, and Linux Kernel Exploits
weekIntro: This week, core identity and network management assets face immediate danger with an actively exploited CVSS 10.0 zero-day in Cisco ISE and a critical unauthenticated root RCE in Check Point Management Servers. Meanwhile, public exploit releases for four Linux kernel privilege escalation flaws and critical vulnerabilities across DNS resolvers and container sandboxes demand urgent patching across your infrastructure.

articles.title: Cisco Issues CVE‑2026‑76460 Zero‑Day, CVSS 10.0, Actively Exploited in ISE API Authentication Bypass
articles.summary: Cisco disclosed a critical authentication‑bypass zero‑day (CVE‑2026‑76460) in its Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE Passive Identity Connector. The flaw allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass the web‑based management interface via an unprotected API endpoint, gaining root‑level command execution. Active exploitation has been confirmed.
articles.impact: Security teams using Cisco ISE risk unauthorized network access and full device compromise, potentially exposing the entire enterprise LAN/WAN to malicious actors.
articles.action: Immediately upgrade all ISE and ISE‑PIC nodes to the latest patched releases and audit access.log for the “dummyuser” indicator, re‑imaging any compromised devices.

articles.title: Critical Check Point Management Server Stack Overflow Allows Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution as Root
articles.summary: A stack‑based buffer overflow in the login routine of Check Point Security Management Server and Log Server (CVE‑2026‑91843) lets unauthenticated attackers send an overlong username and execute arbitrary code with root privileges over the network. Check Point rates the flaw 9.8 CVSS and has issued a LivePatch fix.
articles.impact: Security teams face immediate risk of full system compromise on any vulnerable management or log server, regardless of configuration or VPN usage.
articles.action: Apply the Check Point LivePatch update (advisory SK1000155) and, if patching cannot be done immediately, restrict access to trusted IPs via the SmartConsole Trusted Clients setting.

articles.title: Active Exploitation of WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass (CVE‑2026‑5430) Targets Admin Tokens
articles.summary: A critical JWT authentication bypass in WSO2 API Manager (CVE‑2026‑5430, CVSS 9.8) is being actively exploited in the wild, allowing attackers to forge admin‑level tokens and take over accounts across multiple WSO2 products.
articles.impact: Security teams using vulnerable WSO2 API Manager, Control Plane, Traffic Manager, or Universal Gateway risk immediate unauthorized admin access and full system compromise.
articles.action: Apply the released patches for all affected WSO2 versions immediately and rotate all JWT signing keys.

articles.title: Public Exploits Released for Four Linux Kernel Local‑Root Flaws
articles.summary: Researcher Asim Manizada published working exploit code for four Linux kernel vulnerabilities—DirtyAH6 (CVE‑2026‑80844), TUNderflow (CVE‑2026‑81000), PPPoEject, and DiagSpill—after coordinated patches were released.
articles.impact: Any system still running a pre‑patched kernel is now at immediate risk of local privilege escalation, potentially allowing attackers with low‑privilege accounts to gain full control.
articles.action: Update all Linux servers and workstations to the latest kernel versions released by your distribution without delay.

articles.title: Critical Heap Overflow in Unbound DNSSEC Validator Enables Remote Code Execution (CVE‑2026‑81642)
articles.summary: All Unbound DNS resolver releases prior to 1.26.1 contain a heap overflow in the DNSSEC validator that an attacker can trigger via a malicious DNS zone, allowing remote code execution with a network‑only attack vector.
articles.impact: Exploitable resolvers can be compromised without user interaction, risking full system takeover or service disruption for any infrastructure that relies on Unbound for DNSSEC validation.
articles.action: Upgrade immediately to Unbound 1.26.1 or apply the provided source patches for CVE‑2026‑81642.

articles.title: Critical Docker Sandboxes Flaw (CVE‑2026‑77179) Allows Guest Code to Escape macOS Host Filesystem
articles.summary: Docker Sandboxes versions 0.28.0‑0.41.x on macOS contain a critical vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑77179) that lets malicious code inside a sandbox VM follow symlinks via virtio‑fs, escape the shared project directory, and read or modify any host file with the host account’s privileges.
articles.impact: Security teams must treat any Docker Sandboxes deployment on macOS prior to 0.42.0 as compromised if malicious code runs inside the sandbox, because an attacker can gain full host file system access and potentially execute code as the host user.
articles.action: Upgrade Docker Sandboxes to version 0.42.0 or later immediately and audit host systems for unauthorized file changes.

articles.title: Acronis cPanel Backup Plugin Vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑87886) Exploited in Targeted Attacks
articles.summary: Acronis confirms active exploitation of CVE‑2026‑87886, a high‑severity local privilege escalation flaw in its Backup plugin for cPanel/WHM (Linux) before build 1.9.3.1021 and its Plesk extension before build 1.8.11.638. The CVSS score is 7.
articles.impact: Attackers with low‑privilege access can elevate to root on affected servers, enabling arbitrary code execution and data compromise. Ongoing targeted campaigns indicate the vulnerability is being leveraged in the wild.
articles.action: Apply Acronis 1.9.3 HF3 (or later) immediately to all affected cPanel/WHM and Plesk installations.
affected_systems: Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel & WHM (Linux) before build 1.9.3.1021
Acronis Backup extension for Plesk (Linux) before build 1.8.11.638

articles.title: ISC Releases BIND 9.20.29 and 9.21.26 to Patch 14 Critical Flaws, Including DoH Crash (CVE‑2026‑77692)
articles.summary: The Internet Systems Consortium has issued BIND 9.20.29 and 9.21.26, fixing fourteen vulnerabilities disclosed on 16 September.
articles.impact: Unauthenticated attackers can cause denial‑of‑service on DNS‑over‑HTTPS resolvers and mis‑configured recursive servers, potentially disrupting name resolution for entire networks.
articles.action: Upgrade all BIND installations to 9.20.29 (or later) or 9.21.26 immediately; migrate any remaining 9.18 deployments to a supported branch.

articles.title: PhantomRaven npm Stealer Built with LLM Targets Developers’ CI/CD Secrets
articles.summary: CrowdStrike links a financially motivated actor, posing as a bug bounty hunter, to the PhantomRaven JavaScript stealer distributed via over 100 malicious npm packages.
articles.impact: Security teams must treat npm supply‑chain hygiene as critical, as compromised packages can silently install remote dynamic dependencies that bypass traditional scans and expose CI/CD pipelines.
articles.action: Audit and lock down npm dependencies, enforce strict package signing, and monitor for unauthorized token access in CI/CD environments.

articles.title: Transparent Tribe Deploys Rust‑Based Backdoor Using Private GitHub Repos for C2 in Operation RapidRust
articles.summary: Transparent Tribe (APT36/Earth Karkaddan) launched Operation RapidRust, delivering four new tools—RUSTYSHADE, RUSTYMOVE, PSNATCH, and BASHNATCH—against Indian and Afghan government and defense networks.
articles.impact: Security teams must assume that compromised GitHub credentials can provide stealthy, encrypted command‑and‑control channels, and that both Windows and Linux assets are targeted for data exfiltration and lateral movement.
articles.action: Audit and revoke any unused GitHub tokens, monitor for traffic to private GitHub repositories, and block known typosquatted domains used in the campaign.

articles.title: Plugin4Shell Vulnerability Allows Malicious Plugin Swaps in Four Major AI Coding Agents
articles.summary: A flaw in Anthropic Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Google Gemini CLI lets repository owners replace a locked plugin with malicious code by exploiting branch names that mimic...
articles.impact: Security teams face a risk of credential theft and system compromise whenever an AI coding agent installs a compromised plugin, especially on self‑hosted Git servers or Bitbucket that permit hash‑like branch names.
articles.action: Audit all AI coding agent plugin sources, enforce repository hosting on platforms that block hash‑like branch names (e.g., GitHub), and apply patches from Anthropic and OpenAI immediately.
